choices.where: Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean: the four left-translation ceiling lemmas
choices.pr_choice: Names them Int.ceil_intCast_add, Int.ceil_natCast_add, Int.ceil_one_add and Int.ceil_ofNat_add, mirroring the existing ceil_add_* names.
choices.consequence: Names are the API users search and rewrite with; other names would break the symmetry with Int.ceil_add_intCast and the floor analogues.

choices.pr_choice: Provides the identity for an integer, a natural number, 1 and a numeral literal as four separate lemmas.
choices.status_reason: Item 1 of the capability: the PR proves the natural-number, one and numeral special cases, and special cases the PR covers are requirements to keep.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief lists the special cases (natural number, z = 1, numeral >= 2) because the rules require keeping special cases the PR proves.
choices.consequence: The separate variants exist for syntactic matching by simp and rw; dropping one leaves ⌈1 + a⌉ or ⌈3 + a⌉ unsimplified.

choices.pr_choice: States ⌈z + a⌉ = z + ⌈a⌉ with the integer on the left on both sides and the integer as the first explicit argument.

choices.where: Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean: the four left-translation ceiling lemmas
choices.pr_choice: Tags all four with @[simp].
choices.consequence: Puts them in the default simp set, so simp normalises ⌈z + a⌉ by pulling the integer out; without it callers must name the lemma.

choices.where: Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean: the four left-translation ceiling lemmas

choices.excerpt: file: `Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Floor/Ring.lean`; changed: attributes:added, name:added, proof:added, statement_or_type:added

choices.pr_choice: Adds a public helper characterising 2 * fract x = 1 as 2 * x being an odd integer, used to prove the half-ceiling formula.
choices.consequence: A new public lemma in a widely imported file; it could instead stay private, be inlined, or be phrased through the half-odd-integers.

choices.pr_choice: Names it Int.two_mul_fract_eq_one_iff_exists_int.
Places the helper in Floor/Ring.lean rather than in Round.lean where it is used.
Expresses round x over a ring as (⌊2 * x⌋ + 1) / 2 with integer division, rather than for example ⌊2x⌋ − ⌊x⌋ or ⌊x⌋ + ⌊2 fract x⌋.
choices.excerpt: theorem round_eq' (x : α) : round x = (⌊2 * x⌋ + 1) / 2 := by
choices.consequence: The shape decides which floor API the topology proofs and later users rewrite through, and the PR's own comment floats it as a future definition of round.

choices.pr_choice: Proves the formula over every linearly ordered floor ring (the ring section), not only fields.
choices.excerpt: Formula for `round` in terms of `Int.floor`, a version that works over any ring.
choices.status_reason: Item 2 of the capability: the point of the formula is that it holds without division in α.
choices.visibility_reason: The brief states item 2 as valid in every linearly ordered floor ring; the formula itself is withheld.
choices.consequence: A field-only formula would duplicate round_eq and could not serve the ring-level topology results.

choices.pr_choice: Names the ring formula with a prime, round_eq', beside the field formula round_eq.
choices.consequence: Primed names are hard to discover and say nothing about how the two formulas differ; a descriptive name would be searchable.

choices.pr_choice: Leaves the definition of round unchanged and records only a TODO about adopting the ring formula as the definition.
choices.excerpt: TODO: decide if we want to use this as a definition. It may be slightly faster over `ℚ`. -/
choices.consequence: Changing the definition would alter definitional unfolding for every user of round; deferring keeps behaviour but leaves two formulas.

choices.pr_choice: Adds a public lemma that off the exceptional points round x = ⌈2 * x⌉ / 2, used to identify the left limit.
choices.excerpt: theorem round_eq_half_ceil_two_mul {x : α} (hx : 2 * fract x ≠ 1) : round x = ⌈2 * x⌉ / 2 := by
choices.consequence: A second ring formula in the API; it could be folded into the topology proof or stated case-wise.

choices.pr_choice: Names the half-ceiling formula round_eq_half_ceil_two_mul and the characterisation round_eq_iff.
choices.consequence: round_eq_iff is the name users will look for; another name, or a name like round_eq_iff_mem_Ico, changes discoverability.

choices.pr_choice: States the characterisation as membership in Ico (n - 1 / 2) (n + 1 / 2) with x and n implicit and 1 / 2 rather than 2⁻¹.
choices.excerpt: round x = n ↔ x ∈ Ico (n - 1 / 2 : α) (n + 1 / 2)
choices.consequence: An Ico membership rewrites differently from a conjunction of inequalities. (The brief shows the iff with round x = n on the left, which is the mathematical statement; the encoding stays hidden.)

choices.pr_choice: Proves the characterisation only over linearly ordered fields, with no division-free form over rings.
choices.status_reason: Item 3 of the capability, at least over fields (the PR's case); the ring form is left open in section 4.
choices.visibility_reason: Item 3 is stated in a linearly ordered field; section 4 asks whether a division-free ring form is wanted, so the field-only restriction is visible but not imposed.
choices.consequence: A ring form (2n − 1 ≤ 2x < 2n + 1) would serve ℤ-like floor rings too.

choices.pr_choice: Gives none of the new round lemmas an attribute; round_eq_iff is not simp.
choices.excerpt:
+
+theorem round_eq_iff {x : α} {n : ℤ} : round x = n ↔
choices.consequence: A simp round_eq_iff would fire on every round x = n goal; leaving it off keeps simp's behaviour but requires naming it.

choices.pr_choice: Re-derives round_eq from the ring formula and the three special-value lemmas from the new characterisation by norm_num/simp.
choices.excerpt: theorem round_two_inv : round (2⁻¹ : α) = 1 := by norm_num [round_eq_iff]

choices.pr_choice: Proves the ring formula by splitting x into floor and fractional part, the half-ceiling formula by the parity of 2x, and the characterisation from round_eq.
Writes docstrings for the two ring formulas only; the characterisation and the topology lemmas get none.
choices.excerpt: /-- Away from the points with fractional part `1 / 2`, `round x = ⌈2 * x⌉ / 2`. -/

choices.pr_choice: Removes IsStrictOrderedRing from the section's variables and the omit before tendsto_floor_right_pure_floor, re-adding it after the floor lemmas, so the new floor continuity lemmas do not assume it.
Restates the existing lemmas in place for the integer-valued maps α → ℤ instead of the casts α → α, with no deprecation and no cast-valued version kept.
choices.excerpt:
-    ContinuousOn (fun x => floor x : α → α) (Ico n (n + 1) : Set α) :=
-  (continuousOn_congr <| floor_eq_on_Ico' n).mpr continuousOn_const
+    ContinuousOn (fun x => floor x : α → ℤ) (Ico n (n + 1) : Set α) :=

choices.consequence: Slightly more general; matters only for floor rings that are not strict ordered rings.

choices.where: Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Order/Floor.lean: continuousAt_floor, continuousAt_ceil, the _compl_range lemmas, continuousAt_round, continuousOn_round
choices.pr_choice: States every new continuity result for the maps into ℤ with its discrete topology, not for their casts into α.
choices.excerpt: theorem continuousOn_floor_compl_range : ContinuousOn (floor : α → ℤ) (range Int.cast)ᶜ := by
choices.consequence: Users wanting continuity of the cast-valued map must compose with the cast; the alternative serves analysis users directly but loses generality.

choices.pr_choice: Phrases the non-integer hypothesis as x ≠ ⌊x⌋ for both, so the ceiling lemma's hypothesis is stated through floor.
choices.excerpt: theorem continuousAt_ceil {x : α} (hx : x ≠ ⌊x⌋) : ContinuousAt ceil x :=
choices.consequence: Alternatives (x ∉ range Int.cast, fract x ≠ 0, x ≠ ⌈x⌉ for ceiling) change what callers must prove and how fun_prop discharges side goals.

choices.pr_choice: Expresses the non-integers as the complement of the range of Int.cast.
choices.consequence: Another description of the set (for example {x | fract x ≠ 0}) would need conversion lemmas at use sites.

choices.pr_choice: Encodes one-sided constancy of round as Tendsto to a pure filter along 𝓝[≥] x and 𝓝[<] x, like the existing floor lemmas.

choices.consequence: An eventually-equal or ContinuousWithinAt form would compose differently; the Tendsto-pure form matches the existing floor API.

choices.pr_choice: States the left value uniformly as ⌈2 * x⌉ / 2 rather than case-wise as round x or round x − 1.

choices.pr_choice: Proves one-sided constancy by rewriting with the ring formula and composing the existing one-sided floor limits with doubling, and continuity by splitting into left and right limits.
Adapts continuousOn_fract to the integer-valued floor lemma by composing with the cast's continuity, and reproves continuousAt_fract through the new continuousAt_floor.

feasibility_reason: The task states mathematically: ceiling under left integer translation, a division-free formula for round, the field characterisation of round x = n, continuity of floor and ceiling off the integers, one-sided constancy of round and its continuity off the half-odd-integers. The consequential proposed choices are all withheld: the in-place restatement of continuousOn_floor/continuousOn_ceil (raised neutrally in section 4 with three readings), ℤ-valued versus cast-valued continuity, the shape of the ring formula, the uniform ⌈2x⌉/2 left value, the encodings of the exceptional set and the non-integers, hypotheses, names, simp and fun_prop. What is exposed is required or unavoidable: the ring-level generality of the formula, the field-level characterisation, the natural/one/numeral special cases and the pointwise plus set-level forms (special cases the PR proves), and the choice of existing files (packet). The import maintenance is only partly stateable: without revealing that Round.lean stopped re-exporting a module, the brief can say only that twelve files gain imports for an unstated reason.
brief_omits: Left out on purpose: the helper characterising 2 * fract x = 1 and the half-ceiling formula round x = ⌈2x⌉/2 (both helpers; the second is folded into item 5's left value, stated case-wise); the PR's TODO about making the ring formula the definition of round (comment text the PR writes); the proof changes to continuousOn_fract and continuousAt_fract (listed only as statements to keep, since their proof changes follow from the hidden in-place restatement and the new floor continuity lemma and would hint at them); the in-place restatement as a kind in section 1 (a proposed choice, left to section 4); Round.lean's public-to-private import change and which modules the twelve files import (proposed maintenance choices); the typeclass and section restructuring in the topology file.
